subject: Residency & deletion evidence for ephemeral inference cache + analytics pipeline

Subject: Residency & deletion evidence for ephemeral inference cache + analytics pipeline

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Peregrine's infra team had a follow-up on two narrow but important points for our DPA redline:

1) Ephemeral inference cache: how is the GPU-local / ephemeral KV/prefix cache treated for residency guarantees? Our security team is asking whether entries ever leave the EU (replication, backups, or telemetry exports).

2) Analytics forwarding: you mentioned we can forward usage/telemetry to our analytics tenant. Is that data pseudonymized before it leaves the EU? If not, can Redwood commit to a pseudonymization step or an in-region aggregator?

We need concrete, evidence-backed language to accept the redline. Can you provide:
- a short operational description of the erasure flow for ephemeral caches (timing + triggers),
- the types of audit evidence Redwood can provide (manifests, log excerpts, signed statement), and
- whether you can restrict all cache replication (including snapshots/backups) to EU-only for our account.

Attached is a marked-up excerpt of the DPA where we call out these pieces.

Best,
Samir
Security & Compliance, Peregrine Financial

Attachment: redlined_dpa_v2.docx (redlines, 42KB)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion evidence for ephemeral inference cache + analytics pipeline

Samir — thanks, great questions. Quick summary up front: we can commit to in-region handling for ephemeral cache and provide time-stamped erasure manifests; analytics forwarding can be configured to pseudonymize prior to any cross-region export. Below are the operational details you asked for.

Operational flow (ephemeral cache):
- Cache lifetime: default TTL = 48 hours for inference prefix cache, configurable down to 0 (no caching).
- Erasure trigger: TTL expiry or explicit customer-delete API. Erasure runs in two phases: immediate tombstone (logical delete) + background secure scrub of physical storage within 72 hours (long tail cleanup window for in-flight writes).
- Backups & replication: Redwood does not include ephemeral cache in periodic backups by default. For accounts requiring on-demand snapshotting we can opt-in; otherwise there is no cross-region replication for ephemeral caches.

Audit evidence we can provide:
- Erasure manifest (CSV) with tokenized keys, deletion timestamp, operator id, and SHA256 of manifest signed by Redwood key
- Timestamped internal audit log excerpt showing the scrub job run and bytes freed
- Screenshots of scrub job status (for initial contract stage) or signed certification on request

Analytics forwarding:
- Two modes supported: (1) in-region aggregator: metrics/pseudonymization occurs in EU region, only hashed/pseudonymized records leave region; (2) raw-forwarding: only for customers who explicitly opt-in and sign a separate data-sharing amendment.

I'll attach our cache erase playbook and a short proposed appendix for the DPA. If Peregrine needs stronger language, we can draft a narrow Appendix-C that guarantees in-region handling and an evidence delivery SLA.

Next steps: please confirm whether you want (A) in-region aggregator + standard Appendix-C, or (B) in-region aggregator + explicit prohibition on any cross-border snapshots for ephemeral cache (we'll need to validate with infra but likely doable for dedicated accounts).

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0123

From: Priya Malhotra <pri.m@peregrine.fin>

Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & deletion evidence for ephemeral inference cache + analytics pipeline

Tessa — thanks for the quick reply and the playbook. A couple of immediate redline asks from our legal & infra teams after reading the playbook:

1) Explicit "no cross-border cache replication" clause: Peregrine needs a contractual statement that ephemeral cache entries (and any system snapshots that include ephemeral cache layers) will not be replicated outside the EU without prior written consent.
2) Evidence format: your erasure manifest is promising — we need the manifest to include a per-job signed UUID and a verifiable signature (DocuSign / PKI) that our auditors can validate.
3) Analytics: your in-region aggregator is acceptable but we require pseudonymization to be irreversible (one-way hashing with salt managed by Peregrine) prior to any export.

We've redlined DPA section 3.2 and proposed language for an Appendix-C; see attached. Also please provide a named on-call contact for incidents affecting evidence delivery.

Regards,
Priya Malhotra
Counsel, Peregrine Financial

Attachment: redlined_dpa_v2.docx (updated comments)

Subject: Fwd: Residency & deletion evidence for ephemeral inference cache + analytics pipeline

Folks — forwarding Peregrine's redlines (see Priya's note). They want:
- hard contract: no cross-border replication of ephemeral cache or snapshots that include cache layer,
- signed PKI-backed manifests we can hand to auditors,
- irreversible pseudonymization (salt controlled by Peregrine) before any export.

Can we:
1) commit to a clause that says "Redwood will not replicate ephemeral caches or cache-containing snapshots outside the EU for the account X unless Redwood obtains prior written consent from Customer"? For Dedicated/Private accounts I think this is operationally enforceable; for multi-tenant Hosted accounts we may need to scope it to customer resources only (no global flushes).
2) produce manifests signed with our internal key and provide a verification endpoint (we can consider PKI cert exchange if legal requires it).
3) support Peregrine-managed salt in the pseudonymization pipeline (customer-provided salt stored in KMS) — that seems doable but ops/infra need sign-off.

Draft language suggestion (for Appendix-C) included in attached text; comments inline. If we can agree in principle I'll have Karthik/Laura coordinate an infra verification and a short ops-runbook to attach.

— Tessa

Attachment: proposed_dpa_appendix_cache.txt (suggested wording)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Residency & deletion evidence for ephemeral inference cache + analytics pipeline

Samir / Priya — thanks for the clear asks. After internal review we've prepared an agreed compromise we can put into an Appendix-C:

Summary of proposed contract language (high level):
- In-region handling: Redwood will ensure ephemeral inference caches for Peregrine's account are created and stored only in EU regions (no replication to other regions) unless Peregrine provides prior written consent for cross-region replication.
- Snapshot exclusion: Redwood will exclude ephemeral cache layers from scheduled backups for Peregrine's account by default; explicit opt-in snapshotting must be requested and documented.
- Erasure SLA & evidence: logical tombstone occurs immediately at TTL expiry or API delete; physical scrub completed within 72 hours of tombstone in 99% of cases. Redwood will provide an erasure manifest (signed with Redwood's service key) including job UUID, deletion timestamp, operator id, and manifest signature. We will also publish a verification endpoint for manifests and can coordinate a cert exchange for cryptographic verification.
- Analytics pseudonymization: Redwood will run a one-way hash using a customer-provided salt (managed in the customer's KMS when requested) before any data leaves the EU aggregator. The pipeline will be configurable to support Peregrine-managed salt.
- Evidence delivery: upon request during the term Redwood will supply a signed erasure manifest and a scrub job log excerpt within 5 business days. Extended compliance packages (SOC2 + extended retention of audit logs) are available as an add-on.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached Appendix-C redline (appendix-c-redline.pdf).
- If language looks acceptable, we'll prepare a short ops verification runbook and have infra validate the KMS salt flow for pseudonymization.
- I'll also provide a named on-call contact (security&compliance liaison) and a 24/7 escalation number in the doc for evidence delivery incidents.

If Peregrine wants PKI-level manifest signatures instead of our service key, we can support a certificate exchange and update the verification endpoint.

Appended: appendix-c-redline.pdf (redline), sample erase manifest format (we can produce a test manifest).

Thanks — look forward to your feedback.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
